items.name: Civil status
items.description: The employee's civil status. Mappings are an assumption to be verified by a domain expert.
items.asked_when: Always

needed_by.purpose: Required field 'Civil status' in the registration.

items.required_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"]

items.required_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and spouse_nationality != "Switzerland"

needed_by.purpose: An employee married to a C permit holder living in Switzerland is not subject to source tax.

items.required_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_holds_c_permit == "yes")

items.required_when_expr: subject_to_source_tax and (address_country != "Liechtenstein" or non_return_days_45 == "yes") and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"]

items.asked_when: For each child, if the employee has children

items.required_when_expr: subject_to_source_tax and (address_country != "Liechtenstein" or non_return_days_45 == "yes") and has_children == "yes"

items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_age_status in ["Minor", "Adult in first education"]

items.name: Common household with the other parent

items.asked_when: For a minor child in the household with shared custody, or an adult child in first education in the household
items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_same_household == "yes" and ((child_age_status == "Minor" and child_custody == "Shared custody") or child_age_status == "Adult in first education")
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_same_household == "yes" and ((child_age_status == "Minor" and child_custody == "Shared custody") or child_age_status == "Adult in first education")

items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result.

items.name: Child: parental care (single, child not in household)
items.description: Per minor child not living in the household, for single, divorced, separated or widowed employees: whether they have parental care.
items.asked_when: For a minor child not in the household, if the employee is single, divorced, separated or widowed
items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"

items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_age_status == "Minor" and ((child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no") or (child_same_household == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and child_shared_custody == "yes") or (child_same_household == "no" and civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_parental_care == "yes"))

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result.

items.description: Per child: who makes the larger financial contribution to the child's maintenance - the employee or the other parent.
items.asked_when: If there is alternating custody, or if a single, divorced, separated or widowed employee lives with the child and the other parent in a common household
items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and (child_alternating_custody == "yes" or (civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes"))
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and (child_alternating_custody == "yes" or (civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes"))

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result; the main contributor can count the child (tariff H for single persons).

items.name: Child: more than 50% of maintenance provided

items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_age_status == "Adult in first education" and (child_same_household == "no" or (child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no"))
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_age_status == "Adult in first education" and (child_same_household == "no" or (child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no"))

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result.

items.description: For Germany residents who return daily: whether they have a certificate of residence (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung). 'not yet' is valid and counts as 'no' for the tariff code. The document goes to HR outside Lonio (no upload).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Germany and returns daily

items.asked_when_expr: subject_to_source_tax and address_country == "Germany" and daily_return_germany == "no" and daily_return_reasonable == "yes"
items.required_when_expr: subject_to_source_tax and address_country == "Germany" and daily_return_germany == "no" and daily_return_reasonable == "yes"

rules.name: Questionnaire flow overview
rules.statement: The employee answers the questionnaire in English in these steps and this order. Each piece of information is asked once and reused for every receiving party; a question appears only when at least one party needs it for this person. Swiss residents with Swiss citizenship or a C permit never see source tax questions.

table.then: First name, last name, date of birth - always.
First working day (contractual start date) - always.
Street, house number (or 'no house number'), postcode, town, country, as on the first working day - always; canton only if living in Switzerland.
Only if living in Switzerland: nationality; if not Swiss, whether they hold a C permit.

Civil status - always. Spouse's/partner's date of birth if Married, Registered partnership or Separated. Spouse's nationality, C permit and country of residence only if needed for the spouse exemption (employee in Switzerland, non-Swiss, no C permit, married or registered partnership).
Only if living in Liechtenstein: daily return; if not, more than 45 non-return days. If the answers mean in principle no source tax liability, steps 7 to 9 are skipped.
Only if a tariff code is needed: denomination; spouse gainfully employed if married or registered partnership.

Only if a tariff code is needed: has children; if yes, one block per child (age status, same household, then custody, common household, shared custody / parental care, alternating custody, main contributor, maintenance over 50% as applicable).
Only if living in Germany: daily return; if yes, certificate of residence; if no, daily return reasonable and, if reasonable, more than 60 non-return days.
Permit reminder for non-Swiss employees and everyone living abroad; answers that no longer apply are discarded; after submission the questionnaire is read-only.

rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance start date is derived from the first working day (the contractual start date): if it is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month. It is always derived again from the latest first working day. Assumption on the contractual start date to be verified by a domain expert.

rules.name: Civil status for the pension fund
rules.statement: The civil status entered at the pension fund is the employee's civil status, except that registered partnership and separated are entered as Married (with the spouse's/partner's date of birth). Assumption to be verified by a domain expert.

rules.name: Canton for the pension fund
rules.statement: The pension fund 'Canton' is the canton of residence for employees living in Switzerland; for employees living abroad it is the canton of the place of work, Zurich. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert.

rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee living abroad is subject to source tax whatever their nationality. An employee living in Switzerland is subject only if not Swiss (anyone with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss), without a C permit, and not married or in a registered partnership with a Swiss national or C permit holder who lives in Switzerland. 'Here' in HR's wording means Switzerland. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert.
inputs: Spouse Swiss or C permit holder
rules.expression: address_country != "Switzerland" or (address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and not (civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_holds_c_permit == "yes") and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland"))

rules.name: Liechtenstein: in principle no source tax liability
rules.statement: For an employee living in Liechtenstein who returns daily, or who does not return daily and expects at most 45 non-return days, Lonio records 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code, flagged for HR, and skips the tariff questions. With more than 45 non-return days the normal tariff code is computed with the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert.

table.then: In principle no source tax liability, subject to the DTA; flagged for HR
In principle no source tax liability, subject to the DTA; flagged for HR
Normal tariff code with note 'subject to the double taxation agreement'; flagged for HR

rules.name: Civil status for source tax
rules.statement: For source tax, married and registered partnership count as 'married or registered partnership'; single, divorced, separated and widowed count as 'single'.
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "Married or registered partnership", if_else(is_set(civil_status), "Single, divorced, separated or widowed", null))

rules.name: Residence for source tax
rules.statement: The calculator's residence answer is derived from the country of residence: Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein, or other country. It is not asked separately.

table.then: Other country (base tariff, no further residence questions)

rules.expression: if_else(address_country == "Switzerland", "Switzerland", if_else(address_country == "Germany", "Germany", if_else(address_country == "Liechtenstein", "Liechtenstein", if_else(is_set(address_country), "Other country", null))))

rules.name: Church-tax suffix
rules.statement: The tariff code ends in Y for Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed, and N for none or other.

when: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

rules.expression: if_else(confession == "Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed", "Y", if_else(confession == "None or other", "N", null))

rules.name: Per-child result
rules.statement: Each child gets a result: 'counts', 'counts with H' (single persons only; makes the tariff H) or 'does not count'. Observed calculator rows win over the derived pattern; rows marked inferred are subject to the go-live check against the calculator. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert.
rules.expression: if_else(child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Sole custody", if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "counts", "counts with H"), if_else(child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes", if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "counts", if_else(child_main_financial_contributor == "The employee", "counts with H", "does not count")), if_else(child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no", if_else(child_alternating_custody == "no", if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "does not count", "counts with H"), if_else(child_main_financial_contributor == "The employee", if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "counts", "counts with H"), "does not count")), if_else(child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no", if_else((child_shared_custody == "yes" or child_parental_care == "yes") and child_alternating_custody == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "The employee", if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "counts", "counts with H"), "does not count"), if_else(child_age_status == "Adult in first education" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes", if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "counts", if_else(child_main_financial_contributor == "The employee", "counts with H", "does not count")), if_else(child_age_status == "Adult in first education" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no", if_else(child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes", if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "counts", "counts with H"), "does not count"), if_else(child_age_status == "Adult in first education" and child_same_household == "no" and child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes", "counts", "does not count")))))))

rules.name: Child digit
rules.statement: The child digit of the tariff code is the number of children whose result is 'counts' or 'counts with H'; 0 if the employee has no children. The expression gives each child's contribution (1 or 0), summed over all children. There is no maximum number of children.
rules.expression: if_else(has_children == "yes" and child_result in ["counts", "counts with H"], 1, 0)

rules.name: Base tariff letter
rules.statement: Married employees and registered partners get C if the spouse/partner works or receives replacement income, otherwise B. Single, divorced, separated and widowed employees get H if at least one child counts with H, otherwise A. Tariffs G/Q (replacement income) and special tariffs do not occur. The expression is per child; H applies if any child gives H.
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], if_else(spouse_gainful_employment == "yes", "C", "B"), if_else(child_result == "counts with H", "H", "A"))

rules.name: Cross-border tariff applies
rules.statement: For Germany residents the cross-border tariff applies with daily return and a certificate of residence, or without daily return when daily return is reasonable and no more than 60 non-return days are expected. A certificate answered 'not yet' counts as 'no'. In all other cases the normal tariff applies.
rules.expression: address_country == "Germany" and ((daily_return_germany == "yes" and residence_certificate == "yes") or (daily_return_germany == "no" and daily_return_reasonable == "yes" and non_return_days_60 == "no"))

rules.name: Tariff letter
rules.statement: With the cross-border tariff the base letter is replaced: A by L, B by M, C by N, H by P. Otherwise the base letter is used.
rules.expression: if_else(cross_border_tariff, if_else(base_tariff_letter == "A", "L", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "B", "M", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "C", "N", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "H", "P", null)))), base_tariff_letter)

rules.name: Source tax tariff code
rules.statement: For every employee subject to source tax (and not in principle exempt as a Liechtenstein resident), Lonio computes the full Zurich tariff code: tariff letter, child digit and church-tax suffix written together (e.g. C1Y, L0Y). HR no longer uses the calculator. For Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 non-return days the code carries the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement' and is flagged for HR. It is always derived again from the latest answers. Before go-live a domain expert compares it with the calculator for unexplored paths.

table.then: No tariff code; 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the DTA', flagged for HR
Tariff letter + child digit + church-tax suffix (with DTA note for Liechtenstein residents)

rules.expression: if_else(subject_to_source_tax and not liechtenstein_no_source_tax, [tariff_letter, child_count, church_tax_suffix], null)

rules.name: Permit reminder
rules.statement: At the end of the questionnaire, every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad (whatever their nationality, as it is not asked) is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day. HR words the reminder so that a Swiss citizen living abroad can see it does not apply to them. It collects no data.

rules.name: Discard answers that no longer apply
rules.statement: Answers to questions that no longer apply after the employee changes an earlier answer are discarded on submission; until then they may be kept so going back and forth loses no input.

rules.name: Read-only after submission
rules.statement: After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee. Later changes (move, marriage, new child, certificate of residence handed in later, corrected nationality, changed first working day) are made by HR (later HR-side spec). Every derived result (insurance start date, civil status for the fund and for source tax, subject to source tax, tariff code) is always derived again from the latest answers.

open_questions.question: Does Lonio's computed tariff code match the Zurich calculator for the paths not explored (residence block for A/B/H, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N examples, inferred per-child rows)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lonio now owns the tariff result; unexplored or inferred paths could produce wrong codes.
options: Domain expert compares computed codes with the calculator before go-live
open_questions.recommendation: Non-blocking for the spec, but a go-live condition: domain expert comparison before release.

open_questions.question: How does HR see the Liechtenstein DTA flag and change the first working day or other answers after submission?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Several decisions rely on HR acting after submission; this belongs to the later HR-side spec.
open_questions.recommendation: Note for the later HR-side spec; not blocking the questionnaire.

exclusions.reason: Security changes the badge system next year; may be revisited then.
Not needed by the receiving parties in scope.

exclusions.item: Income type and replacement-income questions (tariffs G/Q)
exclusions.reason: A new employee always has earned income.

exclusions.item: Permit type other than 'holds a C permit'
exclusions.reason: No party needs any other permit type (data minimisation).

exclusions.item: Special tariffs such as D (second job) and calculator-excluded cases (artists, board fees, hardship, pensions)
Transmission of data to receiving parties (exports, portal entry, change notifications)
Starting the onboarding and any HR screens
exclusions.reason: Only the employee side is in scope; HR side specified later.

exclusions.item: Upload of documents (certificate of residence, proof of non-return days, permit)
exclusions.reason: Documents go to HR outside Lonio.
